SailPoint ISC uses the **OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials** grant. Your Personal Access Token's client ID and secret are the credentials for that flow.

## Request

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}
```

Replace `{tenant}` with your org name (e.g. `acme`).

## Examples

**curl**
```bash
curl -s -X POST \
  "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={client_id}&client_secret={client_secret}"
```

**Python (requests)**
```python
import requests

token_url = "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token"

resp = requests.post(token_url, data={
    "grant_type": "client_credentials",
    "client_id": "{client_id}",
    "client_secret": "{client_secret}",
})
resp.raise_for_status()
access_token = resp.json()["access_token"]
```

## Using the token

Pass it as a `Bearer` token on subsequent API calls:

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts
Authorization: Bearer {access_token}
```

## Response shape

```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJ...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 750
}
```

Tokens expire after 750 seconds (12.5 minutes) by default, so you'll need to re-request one when it expires.
